hero.title: Seabourn Mediterranean Cruises
hero.subtitle: Small Ports, Islands & Luxury Itineraries
paragraphs: A Seabourn Mediterranean cruise offers a more intimate way to explore one of the world's most diverse cruising regions.

The Mediterranean combines ancient cities, historic ports, islands, beaches, archaeological sites, renowned cuisine and distinctive cultures. But the appeal of a Seabourn itinerary is not simply how many destinations you can visit.

Seabourn's smaller luxury ships can create opportunities to experience lesser-known ports and smaller coastal destinations alongside major Mediterranean highlights. Depending on the itinerary, travelers may explore destinations across Italy, Greece, Croatia, France, Spain, Turkey and other Mediterranean regions, with itineraries varying by season and year.
This guide explains where Seabourn sails in the Mediterranean, why smaller ports matter, what signature experiences can add to the journey, when to travel and how to choose the right itinerary.

whyTakeSection.title: Why Take a Seabourn Mediterranean Cruise?
whyTakeSection.subtitle: THE APPEAL
paragraphs: The Mediterranean is particularly well suited to small-ship cruising. Many of the region's most memorable experiences are found away from the largest cruise terminals.

A Seabourn voyage combines historic cities, small coastal towns, Greek islands, Italian ports, Croatian villages, French Riviera destinations, Mediterranean cuisine, archaeological sites, beaches, cultural experiences, and scenic cruising.
The result is a trip that can feel more like a luxury exploration of the Mediterranean than a traditional port-intensive cruise.
whyTakeSection.conclusion: The result is a trip that feels like a private luxury yacht exploration of the Mediterranean rather than a conventional commercial cruise.

differentCards.title: What Makes Seabourn Mediterranean Cruises Different?
differentCards.subtitle: SMALL SHIPS, BIGGER DISCOVERY
paragraphs: One of Seabourn's biggest advantages in the Mediterranean is the size and atmosphere of its ships. A smaller ship can make certain destinations feel more intimate. This makes Seabourn especially attractive to travelers who have already visited the major Mediterranean capitals and want to explore beyond the obvious stops.

historySection.heading: Seabourn Mediterranean for History Lovers
historySection.subtitle: MILLENNIA OF CIVILIZATION
paragraphs: The Mediterranean is one of the world's richest regions for history. A single voyage can span millennia of human triumph, art, and architectural genius.
The distinct advantage of cruising aboard a Seabourn small ship is the ability to move seamlessly between major historical eras and civilizations without ever changing hotels or packing a suitcase.
highlights: Ancient Greece & the cradle of Western democracy
The grandeur of Ancient Rome & imperial monuments
Byzantine mosaics, basilicas, and sacred architecture
Ottoman palaces, grand bazaars, and minarets
Medieval European fortified castles and ramparts
Italian Renaissance art, palaces, and sculpture
Phoenician, Venetian, and Knights of St. John maritime history

items.title: Regional Mediterranean Flavors
items.subtitle: Italy • Greece • Croatia • France • Spain
items.description: Each Mediterranean country brings a distinct culinary identity. A Seabourn voyage allows travelers to savor authentic dishes both ashore in family-owned trattorias and onboard through destination-inspired menus crafted with locally sourced market ingredients.
items.bestFor: Handmade pasta and white truffles in Italy, fresh grilled sea bass and kalamata olive oils in Greece, black risotto and plavac wine in Croatia, bouillabaisse and artisanal cheeses in Provence, authentic tapas and jamón ibérico in Spain.

items.title: Legendary Mediterranean Wine Regions
items.subtitle: Tuscan Coast • Provence • Santorini • Dalmatia • Catalonia
items.description: The Mediterranean cradle boasts Europe's most storied vineyards. Seabourn incorporates sommelier-led tastings and private estate excursions to give guests exclusive access to historic cellars.
items.bestFor: Crisp Assyrtiko from Santorini volcanic soils, elegant Provençal rosés overlooking the sea, bold Super Tuscans and Chiantis, indigenous Plavac Mali on the Dalmatian coast, and sparkling Catalan Cavas.

bestFor: Intimate small-ship luxury atmosphere with only 450–600 guests
Access to boutique small ports and secluded islands unreachable by mega-ships
World-class Mediterranean dining and destination-inspired regional menus
Inclusive luxury model covering open-bar drinks, fine wines, Wi-Fi, and gratuities
All-suite accommodations with expansive private verandas
Exclusive signature experiences such as private concerts at ancient Ephesus
Complimentary watersports from the retractable marina in sheltered bays
Docking directly in historic town centers rather than industrial freight docks
Sophisticated, relaxed ambiance ideal for couples and culture enthusiasts
notBestFor: Higher upfront fare than mainstream mass-market cruise lines
Popular marquee ports (e.g., Santorini, Dubrovnik) can still be busy during summer
Summer temperatures in southern Mediterranean ports can be very warm
Smaller ships do not feature massive casinos, waterparks, or large theater revues

faqs.question: Where does Seabourn cruise in the Mediterranean?
faqs.answer: Seabourn Mediterranean itineraries can include destinations in Italy, Greece, Croatia, France, Spain, Turkey and other Mediterranean regions, depending on the specific sailing.

faqs.question: What makes Seabourn Mediterranean cruises different?
faqs.answer: Seabourn focuses on an intimate luxury experience with smaller ships, personalized service, sophisticated dining and itineraries that can include smaller ports.

faqs.question: Does Seabourn visit small Mediterranean ports?
faqs.answer: Selected Seabourn itineraries include smaller ports and less-commercialized destinations, although the exact ports vary by voyage.

faqs.question: What are the best Seabourn Mediterranean itineraries?
faqs.answer: The best itinerary depends on your interests. Greece and the Greek islands are ideal for island scenery and history, Italy for art and food, Croatia for the Adriatic, and France and Spain for culture and cuisine.

faqs.question: What is the best time for a Seabourn Mediterranean cruise?
faqs.answer: Late spring and early fall can provide an attractive combination of comfortable temperatures and fewer peak-season crowds. Summer is ideal for travelers prioritizing beach weather and long daylight.

faqs.question: Is summer too hot for a Mediterranean cruise?
faqs.answer: Summer can be very warm, particularly in southern Mediterranean destinations. Travelers focused on sightseeing may prefer spring or fall.

faqs.question: Does Seabourn offer Mediterranean Signature Events?
faqs.answer: Seabourn offers distinctive Signature Experiences and special destination programming, with availability depending on the itinerary.

faqs.question: Are shore excursions included on Seabourn?
faqs.answer: Shore excursions are not universally included simply because you are sailing with Seabourn. The exact inclusions depend on the voyage and excursion selected.

faqs.question: Is Seabourn Mediterranean good for couples?
faqs.answer: Yes. The combination of intimate ships, scenic destinations, fine dining and sophisticated service makes Seabourn particularly appealing for couples.

faqs.question: Is Seabourn Mediterranean good for first-time cruisers?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Mediterranean offers a wide range of destinations, making it an excellent introduction to luxury cruising.

faqs.question: Is Seabourn Mediterranean good for families?
faqs.answer: It can work for multigenerational families, particularly those interested in culture, history and food. Families seeking extensive children's entertainment may prefer a larger cruise ship.

faqs.question: What should I pack for a Seabourn Mediterranean cruise?
faqs.answer: Pack lightweight clothing, comfortable walking shoes, sun protection, a light jacket and smart-casual evening clothing.

faqs.question: Is a balcony worth it on a Mediterranean cruise?
faqs.answer: A balcony can be valuable for enjoying scenic cruising, coastal views, morning coffee and quiet time in port.

faqs.question: Can you combine Italy and Greece on a Seabourn cruise?
faqs.answer: Yes, depending on the itinerary. Some Mediterranean voyages combine multiple countries and regions.

faqs.question: Does Seabourn cruise the Greek Islands?
faqs.answer: Yes, Greek islands can feature on Seabourn Mediterranean itineraries, with the exact destinations depending on the sailing.

faqs.question: Is Seabourn better than a large Mediterranean cruise ship?
faqs.answer: It depends on your priorities. Seabourn is better suited to travelers seeking intimacy, personalized service and luxury, while large ships offer more entertainment and onboard facilities.

faqs.question: Is Seabourn Mediterranean all-inclusive?
faqs.answer: Seabourn offers an inclusive luxury experience with many onboard amenities included, although specific inclusions and optional expenses vary by sailing.

faqs.question: Is a Seabourn Mediterranean cruise worth the money?
faqs.answer: For travelers who value smaller ships, personalized service, excellent dining and distinctive Mediterranean experiences, Seabourn can be worth the premium.

finalVerdict.title: Is Seabourn Mediterranean Right for You?
finalVerdict.subtitle: FINAL VERDICT
paragraphs: Seabourn Mediterranean cruises are an excellent choice for travelers who want to explore the Mediterranean without sacrificing intimacy, luxury or personalized service. The region's combination of ancient history, beautiful islands, small ports, cuisine, wine, beaches and cultural experiences provides extraordinary variety.

Seabourn adds a smaller-ship environment and the opportunity to experience destinations at a more relaxed pace. For travelers who would rather spend the afternoon exploring a historic village or enjoying a quiet Mediterranean harbor than participating in a large-ship entertainment program, Seabourn offers a compelling alternative.
finalVerdict.recommendation: Our recommendation: If your ideal Mediterranean vacation combines small ports, excellent food, cultural discovery, elegant accommodations and distinctive experiences, a Seabourn Mediterranean cruise deserves serious consideration.
